# WorkstationTabOverflowCapNL measures a collapsed reveal's pin strip, because the heavy header it documents no longer stages a cap

## The Symptom

`WorkstationTabOverflowCapNL` fails on `dev` at the staging guard:

```
Error: the heavy header must stage a multi-action trailing partition
expect(received).toBeGreaterThan(expected)
  Expected: > 1
  Received:   1
```

Two mechanisms were proposed and both are dead. @neo-opus-vega bisected it: the same failure reproduces byte-identically against `ac93c04e3c`, the commit immediately before `#18306`, so `HeaderActionPolicy` is exonerated. Vega then hypothesised nesting — actions wrapped one level deeper would stop matching the spec's `:scope >` query while the count collapsed with nothing removed. That is also falsified, below.

## What the DOM Actually Contains

Probed the live app at the spec's own viewport (1180×840). Eight `.neo-tab-header-toolbar` elements:

| kind | actions | capped | overflow ctrl | tabs | clientW | scrollW | activeW |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| reveal | 1 | **1** | – | 1 | **0** | 0 | 0 |
| reveal | 1 | **1** | – | 1 | **0** | 0 | 0 |
| header | 1 | 0 | – | 1 | 180 | 180 | 58 |
| header | 1 | 0 | – | 1 | 413 | 413 | 78 |
| header | 2 | 0 | ✔ | 1 | 276 | 276 | 149 |
| header | 1 | 0 | – | 2 | 220 | 220 | 55 |
| header | 1 | 0 | – | 1 | 220 | 220 | 63 |
| header | 1 | 0 | – | 1 | 1156 | 1156 | 114 |

Nesting is out: `:scope > .neo-toolbar-action` and `.neo-toolbar-action` return the same count on every toolbar. Nothing moved deeper.

Three facts decide it:

1. **No header overflows.** `scrollWidth === clientWidth` on all six. The widest active tab is 149px in a 276px strip. The docblock's premise — *"twelve canonical titles in a narrow pane"* — is not what the app boots into; every header holds one or two tabs.
2. **No heavy header carries a cap.** `.neo-tab-overflow-capped` count is zero on all six.
3. **The only capped elements in the document are the titles of two collapsed reveal headers, and they are zero-width.** A reveal has exactly one trailing action — the pin — by design.

## The Mechanism

`document.querySelector('.neo-tab-overflow-capped')` returns the first match in document order. The heavy headers stage none, so it returns a **collapsed reveal's title**, and every downstream measurement — `toolbar`, `actions`, `clusterWidth`, the cap identity — describes the reveal's one-pin strip instead of the heavy header's trailing cluster. `actionCount === 1` is then the correct answer to the wrong question, which is why no source change explains it and why it predates `#18306`.

This is also why the loud-failure guard did not fire. Its message reads *"if no cap exists, the stage no longer exercises this branch and the spec must fail loudly"* — but a cap **did** exist. A selector that substitutes a different surface defeats a guard written against absence.

## Why It Matters Beyond This Spec

The spec depends on an app's incidental boot composition to stage its degenerate case. When the composition drifted, the spec did not report a missing stage; it silently retargeted and reported a product defect that does not exist — costing two peers a bisect and a mechanism hunt tonight.

The same shape plausibly explains the three `WorkstationPaletteBridgeNL` timeouts, which wait for a **visible** `.neo-tab-header-button` while the capped candidates measure zero width. **Stated as the next thing to check, not as a finding** — no probe has been run against that spec.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The spec stages the over-wide active tab itself rather than inheriting it from app boot defaults.
- [ ] Its capped-button selection cannot resolve to a reveal header, and cannot resolve to a zero-width element.
- [ ] With the stage absent, the spec fails naming the missing stage — verified by removing the staging step and reading the message, not by inspection.
- [ ] The `actionCount > 1` guard measures the surface the assertions then use; a red states which header it measured.
- [ ] Re-running against `ac93c04e3c` no longer reproduces the failure, closing Vega's bisect.

## Out of Scope

- Whether the app *should* boot a twelve-title narrow pane. The spec must not depend on the answer either way.
- `WorkstationPaletteBridgeNL` and `WorkstationStarvedGeometryNL`, which stay unowned until probed.
- The GPU exclusion of this tier from CI — that is `#18408`.

## Related

- `#18306` — exonerated by bisect; recorded so the next reader does not re-open it.
